messages:
maria: Quick heads-up, found a mismatch between per-tier rollout scope and our fallback selector. Repro in thread, want alignment before any runtime change.
aj: What's the concrete issue? TL;DR please.
maria: TL;DR: Tiered canary (model-v2-canary) for paid customers gets fallbacked during load to a cheap compatible model (model-v1-small). That bypasses the rollout scope and serves lower-quality models to paying customers.
kevin: Wait 12; fallback shouldn't ignore scope. I thought `rollout.scope` was always enforced.
maria: Current flow: pick pool by (region, tier), then sample for canary within pool. If fallback fires, compatibility ranking runs and picks any compatible model in-region, regardless of rollout scope.
sophie: This matches a support case I saw 12 where Tier A customers saw quality drop during a spike.
ranjit: Two trade-offs: safety (honor scope even on fallback) vs cost/availability (forcing high-cost fallbacks could blow committed spend).
ui-ux: From the console POV customers expect "who sees the canary" to be a strong guarantee. They are surprised if a fallback gives them a smaller model.
aj: Proposal 1: Make fallback respect rollout.scope. Only consider fallback candidates that are within the same scope (tier + region). If none: either fail the request or surface a clear degradation.
kevin: Proposal 2: Keep global fallback for availability, but emit explicit telemetry and console warnings when we breach scope. That preserves uptime but increases transparency.
ranjit: Also must check entitlement & quota. If fallback routes to a model not licensed for that tier, thats a hard no. Current entitlement check only validates the primary target.
maria: Agreed. Entitlement checks must be part of candidate filtering before any route decision.
aj: API change required: route_request should include rollout_id; router uses that to fetch scope constraints. Alternatively, include scope in-request but that leaks more surface area.
kevin: Pseudocode for selector patch:
`````
fallback_candidates = find_compatible_variants(request.model)
filtered = filter_by_scope_and_entitlement(fallback_candidates, request.rollout.scope, request.tier)
if filtered.empty():
  if request.rollout.fail_closed: return error_response(\"scope_no_candidates\")
  else:
    global = choose_global_fallback(fallback_candidates)
    return rank_by_latency_cost(global)
else:
  return rank_by_latency_cost(filtered)
`````
sophie: Console UX: add rollout toggle with options: "fail closed" vs "allow global fallback". Show a small badge that tracks scope breaches and counts over 7d.
ui-ux: Also show per-tier telemetry: percent of Tier X routed to canary vs scoped fallback vs global fallback. Simple sparkline OK.
ranjit: Telemetry events we need: route_chosen, fallback_trigger, fallback_filtered_by_scope, entitlement_violation. Fields: route_id, rollout_id, tier, region, reason_code, latency_ms, token_count, fallback_variant.
aj: Quotas 12 move enforcement earlier: admission gate should compare request budget against candidate cost profile so we avoid routing to an unaffordable variant.
kevin: Perf note: per-request scope filtering must be cheap. Add rollout->allowed_variants cache keyed by (rollout_id, tier, region) with TTL and control-plane invalidation on rollout updates. Cache lookup O(1).
maria: We'll maintain an in-memory rollout index in the router and invalidate via control-plane events.
ops-bot: deploy scheduled: routing-fallback-scope-proto -> canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC :rocket:
aj: QA checklist:
- unit tests for selector with scoped vs global fallback
- integration test with entitlement mismatch (tier blocked)
- telemetry emitted with fallback_reason and surfaced in console
- perf test: added p95 latency < 1ms
sophie: Logging: add a single compact structured log line for scoped-fallback decisions. Keep fields small for volume control.
kevin: API debate: pass rollout_id only vs full scope blob. I prefer rollout_id to avoid expanding SDK payloads. Router has the metadata cache anyway.
ranjit: Agreed, rollout_id approach minimizes surface area.
ui-ux: Console should call out when scope filters cause failure or deeper degradation so users can toggle behavior intentionally.
maria: Action items:
- kevin: PR for selector + cache (runtime) 12 ETA EOD
- aj: control-plane API: add `fail_closed` toggle on rollouts 12 ETA tomorrow
- ranjit: telemetry schema + cost profile changes 12 PR by Wed
- sophie: console mockups for scope-breach indicator 12 by Fri (figma link below)
- qa: add rollout-scope test matrix into staging runs
kevin: Default plan: `allow-global-fallback` for now, but emit strong telemetry and console hits. Enterprise customers can set `fail_closed`.
maria: I'll draft RFC with exact API shapes and test matrix and link back.
aj: +1. Tag me for API review.
sophie: mockup: https://figma.redwood/redwood/canary-scope-breach-mockup
maria: RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/1891-canary-scope-fallback
ranjit: Add to support playbook: interpret fallback_reason codes and mitigation steps.
kevin: One more: cross-region routing 12 if rollout is region-limited and no same-region candidate exists, we must consult data-residency policy before routing cross-region. Add residency check to filter step.
maria: Added.
ops-bot: Reminder: staging canary window 03:00-04:00 UTC.
maria: Thanks all, closing thread. I'll attach RFC and PR links when ready.
